cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Brighter Side
cards.instruction: Meet every setback with even greater optimism.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No tickets sold for our show. I've approved an uninterrupted rehearsal; you may enjoy the privacy.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I get our deposit back? The theatre's cancelled us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Refund pursuit is approved. Even better, we'll hire the pub upstairs; it comes with people already in it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They've kept the deposit. Can we just take the bus home? That's all we can afford.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A touring production is approved! I'll carry the scenery. You may begin the opening scene between stops; we've finally got a moving audience.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 grants rehearsal privacy, A3 approves refund pursuit as a better venue chance, and A5 authorizes touring from a request to go home.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 cancellation causes A3 pub plan; B4 no refund and bus-only money cause A5 transport-based performance.

relationship.evidence: B2 seeks funds and B4 asks to stop spending, plausibly managing a production loss while A keeps reinterpreting it.

heightening.evidence: B4 removes the venue budget and A5 enlarges the imagined show into touring with a moving audience.

specificity.evidence: A1 failed sales, B2 cancellation and B4 remaining bus fare make the worsening situation legible.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 moving audience follows the bus constraint, though actual passengers are a prospective assumption rather than confirmed attendees.
